initialBudgetRationale: Re-baselined to the measured Nuxt 4.5 graph (235.95 kB initial, 202.69 kB JavaScript) plus about 1 kB of headroom, and CI now enforces these caps instead of warning. The previous 229 / 192.5 caps were set during the Nuxt 4.5 adoption before the graph was re-measured; the build had exceeded them ever since while CI only warned, so they described an intention rather than the build and caught no regression. An enforced cap at the real number protects against the next regression; ratchet it back down as bytes are recovered. docs/perf-initial-graph.md records the measured composition and the candidate levers, none of which clear the old cap on their own. The 0.1 kB above 237 is tolerance for chunk-hash churn, not new code: the entry and preload map list every lazy chunk by content hash, and those hashes do not compress, so changing any lazy-only component moves the initial gzip size by a few bytes. Splitting App/Header, Media/Video and Edit/Presentation (none of which are in the initial graph) moved it from 237.00 to 237.01 kB.
